title: 3-Read Friday #34: England Travelogue, Conceptual Understanding, and Revision Resources
author: Craig Barton
summary: Issue #34 covers a school-visit reflection, a debate on conceptual understanding, and revision resources. Doug Lemov recaps his visit to Ark Soane Academy, where he observed Pritesh Raichura's 'three phases of questioning' technique for building attention, rehearsal, and checking for understanding. Jemma Sherwood challenges the common assumption that explaining why a procedure works is equivalent to conceptual understanding, arguing the two are related but distinct. Colleen Young rounds out the issue with a curated list of GCSE and A-Level revision resources. Barton frames Lemov's account of the questioning model as the most fascinating item, given his own interest in attention and memory-building techniques.
points: Barton singles out Lemov's account of Pritesh Raichura's 'three phases of questioning' -- designed to build attention, rehearsal, and checking for understanding -- as the item he finds 'most fascinating.'
He frames Sherwood's post as reframing a 'classic' debate: understanding why a procedure works is not the same thing as conceptual understanding.
He flags Young's revision-resource roundup as useful late-season GCSE/A-Level prep material, 'for the maths geeks.'
